run.runNote: Phase 1 Step 1-2 (source exploration + candidate extraction query generation only; no CodeQL execution, no LLM labeling in this round per the task contract) against the pymodbus_vuln source tree. WORKFLOW.md confirms Pass 1 = CWE-022/023/036/073 Path Traversal with pass query name Pass1_PathTraversal.ql. The CodeQL database pymodbus-db sits INSIDE the source tree, so all exploration, file traversal, and evidence collection excluded pymodbus-db. The database sourceLocationPrefix matches the explored tree (creation sha 927fa4d4d9ddf1ffaa9a6d83616bc4a279f74555, CLI 2.25.1, baseline 19100 LOC), so file/line evidence below refers to the same snapshot the database was built from. Ground-truth-looking artifacts present in the source tree (VULNERABILITY_AUDIT_REPORT.md, path_traversal_sinks.csv, Chinese audit reports) were NOT read, per the experiment independence rule.

target.projectDescription: Modbus protocol library (client/server, TCP/UDP/TLS/serial) with a datastore simulator that embeds an aiohttp web console, an argparse simulator entry point, and typer-based REPL client/server CLIs. The audit-relevant file surface is small and concentrated: the simulator HTTP server (pymodbus/server/simulator/http_server.py) serves static files from a fixed web directory, reads an operator-supplied JSON setup file, and imports an optional custom-actions module; the REPL server reads a typer-supplied config path; the logging helper can open a caller-supplied log file; the TLS layers pass operator-supplied cert/key paths to ssl; the serial layers pass device strings to pyserial; one contrib example rewrites a caller-supplied log file in place.

referenceFilesNotAvailable: references/aiohttp.md - no aiohttp framework reference exists in Augur references/ (available: aspnet, csharp, django, echo, express, fastapi, flask, gin, go, java, javascript, python, spring); framework-specific source/sink shapes were therefore derived from the repository code itself per WORKFLOW.md 4.2.3 fallback

httpHandlers.sourceNode: request.path[1:] (http_server.py:260) - the aiohttp request path (percent-decoded), first character stripped, assigned to 'page' (defaults to 'index.html' when empty)
httpHandlers.flow: page -> os.path.join(self.web_path, page) (http_server.py:262) -> open(file, encoding='utf-8') (:264) and web.FileResponse(file) (:265)
httpHandlers.webBase: self.web_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), 'web') (http_server.py:166) - fixed package-relative base directory
httpHandlers.guardEvidence: NO path containment validation, no basename extraction, no '..' rejection, no realpath/abspath/normpath anywhere in the handler. The only filtering is (a) the route regex {tail:[a-z0-9.]*} which restricts the aiohttp route-matched tail to lowercase letters, digits and dots (no '/' and no uppercase, so '..' as a full segment cannot appear in the matched tail, but a bare dotted name like 'a..b' or hidden files can) - note the handler reads request.path directly rather than request.match_info['tail'], so route-regex protection vs. raw-path access is a labeling/analysis question; and (b) FileNotFoundError/IsADirectoryError -> HTTPNotFound (:266-267). aiohttp request.path is percent-decoded; whether encoded traversal sequences (e.g. %2e%2e%2f) can reach the handler past route matching depends on the aiohttp version's matching behavior (aiohttp not in DB - unresolved, see uncoveredCases).

Modbus 'file record' PDUs (pymodbus/file_message.py, function codes 0x14/0x15 Read/Write File Record) are in-protocol register files, NOT filesystem access - verified: no open/os/pathlib usage in file_message.py.

getpass passwords, env vars: no os.environ reads on path-like values anywhere in the package (only os.urandom at http_server.py:628); no message-queue consumers; no multipart upload handling; no zipfile/tarfile/extractall usage anywhere in the tree.

uncoveredCases: aiohttp is not part of the CodeQL database: web.FileResponse's internal file open/read cannot be traced (the sink row anchors the call site at http_server.py:265 only); request.path percent-decoding and route-regex matching semantics (raw vs decoded path) are external-library behavior - the labeling/analysis step must decide whether the {tail:[a-z0-9.]*} route regex plus the request.path[1:] handler read constitutes a reachable traversal channel.

The handler reads request.path directly instead of request.match_info['tail']; route registrations (web.get/web.post at http_server.py:170-173, reactive/main.py:234) are textual evidence only and are NOT emitted as candidate rows.

request.query (http_server.py:272), await request.post() (:288) and await request.json() (reactive/main.py:279) are real untrusted inputs but are not used to locate files anywhere in this snapshot - documented, not emitted as source rows.

importlib.import_module(custom_actions_module) (http_server.py:140) - module import by caller-supplied name; relevant to code-injection (pass 4) rather than path traversal, and importlib is not a direct filesystem API - not emitted as a sink row; the custom_actions_module parameter IS emitted as a source param row.

self.log_file = log_file (http_server.py:162) and the --log_file CLI option are stored but never consumed in this snapshot (no FileHandler call site on them) - no sink row possible; the log_file param is still emitted as a source row for boundary documentation.
tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile (explain.py:141-143) creates an internal temp path (not attacker-controlled); only the surrounding open/copyfile/os.remove rows are emitted.
request.urlopen (examples/contrib/explain.py:83) is an outbound HTTP fetch (SSRF-relevant pass 3), not a filesystem sink - not emitted for pass 1.

No sanitizer families were observed for path handling: no realpath/abspath/normpath/relative_to/startswith/'..' rejection anywhere on the static-file path (the route regex at http_server.py:172 is the only filter); no TOCTOU-relevant exists()-then-open windows on attacker-controlled paths (the open() at :264 is wrapped in try/except FileNotFoundError, single-shot read).
